newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close higher, U.S. rate hike discounted.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close higher, U.S. rate hike discounted.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed higher with the U.S interest rate hike announced overnight discounted by the market, dealers and analysts said.
"It was a non-event. Everybody had been expecting a rate increase," said Phuah Lee Kerk, head of research at Jupiter Securities.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended up 8.25 points at 1,225.59, while the all-share EMAS index was 3.76 points higher at 359.55.
Analysts said investors were now focussing their attention on the Malaysia's central bank annual report due out on Friday.

They said investors would be looking for any hint about Bank Negara's future monetary policy. There has been speculation that the central bank may raise the statutory reserve requirement of banks to mop up excess funds in the banking system, they said.
"People don't want to take risk ahead of the report. We should see a more positive sentiment next week," Phuah said.
At the close, market volume stood at 427 million shares valued at 2.9 billion ringgit. Gainers overwhelmed losers 509 to 124.
